prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 服务器安全基线核查记录 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 8 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "受检服务器唯一编号" · longest unbreakable word 20px · one-line width 138px
  col 2: header "系统账户口令强度" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 3: header "外部网络访问开放" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 4: header "日志留存天数达标" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 123px
  col 5: header "漏洞补丁更新状态" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 6: header "高危端口关闭数量" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 7: header "近三十天告警次数" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 8: header "应急联系人确认情况" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 138px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1B: widths [54, 51, 51, 51, 38, 38, 38, 38] · table 360×441px · row heights [222, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 8/8 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [51, 38, 38, 54, 51, 38, 38, 51] · table 360×441px · row heights [222, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 8/8 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2A: widths [51, 51, 39, 51, 39, 39, 38, 51] · table 360×441px · row heights [222, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 8/8 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [53, 50, 37, 50, 37, 37, 37, 53] · table 355×418px · row heights [199, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 8/8 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [51, 41, 41, 51, 41, 41, 42, 51] · table 360×441px · row heights [222, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 8/8 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3A: widths [53, 41, 40, 50, 40, 41, 41, 53] · table 360×418px · row heights [199, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 8/8 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3B: widths [55, 40, 39, 51, 40, 39, 39, 56] · table 360×418px · row heights [199, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 8/8 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3C: widths [58, 39, 39, 50, 39, 40, 41, 53] · table 360×418px · row heights [199, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 8/8 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

log.raw: {"preferred":["r3B"],"acceptable":["r3A","r3C","r2B"],"bad":[{"design":"r1B","why":"Last column is only 38px, so the 9-character header stacks into 9 lines and forces a 222px header row while the first column has spare width; the table looks lopsided and unnecessarily tall."},{"design":"r1C","why":"The first column at 51px cannot fit two CJK characters per line, so the 9-character row header alone drives the header row to 9 lines/222px despite width being available elsewhere."},{"design":"r2A","why":"The last column at 51px misses the two-character threshold, producing a 9-line header and a 222px header row; col 2 is also over-wide for a simple yes/no column."},{"design":"r2C","why":"Columns 1 and 8 at 51px both force 9-line headers, making the header row 222px tall; the extra width on col 4 does not compensate for the wasted vertical space."}],"contrast":null,"ranges":[[53,60],[37,45],[37,45],[49,55],[37,45],[37,45],[37,45],[53,60]],"rationale":"This is a narrow phone table where the long 8–9-character CJK headers, not the short cell values, determine height. r3B uses the full 360px and puts the extra width where it changes line breaks: 55–56px for the 9-character first and last headers, 51px for col 4 so the 28px numeric token stays intact, and 39–40px for the peer yes/no columns. That reduces the header row from 222px to 199px without mid-word splits while keeping a clear, balanced rhythm.","principles":{"general":["In narrow CJK tables, header line count often controls row height more than cell content; spend width on columns whose headers can cross a two-character line-break threshold.","Peer columns with the same role and similar content should share width; making one binary column wider creates a false hierarchy.","Numeric columns need at least the longest unbreakable token plus padding before aesthetic balancing."],"specific":["At 15px with 21px padding, 53px is the practical threshold for a 9-character Chinese header to fit two glyphs per line and avoid a 9-line stack.","Column 4 needs at least 49px for the 28px '365' string; 51px gives a little safety.","The middle yes/no columns can stay at 39–40px because their longest unbreakable token is only 16px.","Both the first and last columns have 9-character headers, so both deserve extra width; widening only one leaves the other as the height driver."]},"tradeoffs":"r2B keeps the shorter 199px header row but over-allocates col 2 relative to its yes/no peers and leaves 4px unused; r3C avoids the tall header but makes col 1 noticeably wider than col 8.
